# SpicyAPI Studio Bridge

> MIT-licensed local MCP connection between Spicy Studio and the user's own assistant app: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI or another local stdio MCP client. Version 0.2.2 is a GitHub preview package, not an npm release.

## Facts

- Maintainer: SpicyAPI. Not an OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor or Google product or endorsement.
- Purpose: exchange a selected creative request and a reviewable text or structured short-drama draft.
- Setup: Node.js 22.13+ and a local assistant app. Guided setup for Codex and Claude Code (official login check and official mcp add) and for Cursor and Gemini CLI (one spicy-studio entry in their settings file, with a backup). For Codex the wizard also sets default_tools_approval_mode = "approve" on the spicy-studio entry only (with a backup), so codex exec can call the tools; the global approval policy is unchanged. Other stdio MCP clients use a printed entry. No SpicyAPI API key is required.
- Browser: same computer, exact allowed origin, one-use pairing, fixed loopback port 47321 opened on the first tool call. Only one assistant session holds it at a time; a refreshed page pairs again with studio_connect reset: true. Browser policy may block local access.
- Execution: the user sends a message in the assistant app. Website submission does not start an assistant turn automatically. studio_next_request accepts wait_seconds (0-50, default 0) and waits for a shared request without polling; an empty answer tells the assistant to call again with wait_seconds set to 30 until a request arrives or the user asks it to stop.
- Costs: the assistant app's subscription allowance or API billing applies. The bridge adds no SpicyAPI fee; it grants no free or unlimited model access.
- Media: no image, video, audio or paid model-execution tool. Studio media generation requires a separate selected platform model and price confirmation.
- Privacy: selected request data in memory; no credential-file reader or Studio-history fetch. The assistant's model may process the shared request through its provider.
- Cancellation: stops accepting the result; stop the assistant turn separately to stop its usage.

## Project documentation

- [README and FAQ](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-studio-bridge/blob/main/README.md): setup, package comparison, protocol and limits.
- [Quick start](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-studio-bridge/blob/main/delivery/START-HERE.md): extract the named desktop ZIP and open the OS launcher.
- [Latest release](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-studio-bridge/releases/latest): use the named SpicyAPI-Studio-Bridge ZIP, not the source archive.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-studio-bridge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): changes per version.
- [Verification](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-studio-bridge/blob/main/TESTING.md): simulated CLI and real local MCP/HTTP checks; no real subscription-writing validation or Windows/Linux physical desktop validation.
- [Security](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-studio-bridge/blob/main/SECURITY.md): reporting and local pairing boundaries.
- [Separate SpicyAPI MCP server](https://github.com/Spicy-API/spicy-mcp): API-key-based platform model quoting and generation; not this bridge.
